observations: Photo 0: a white and pink domestic free-arm sewing machine with stitch selector dials and a stitch-length panel; faint brand text on the front, possibly 'Riccar', not clearly legible; fabric tape under the presser foot.
Photo 1: a different white compact domestic sewing machine; front reads 'Semco' and 'indigo 6'; a Singer 'Computer' machine visible behind it.
Photo 2: a third, different white domestic sewing machine; front reads 'NOVAMATIC' and 'NM 868A', with German and French labels (Knopfloch, Stichlange).
All three photos carry a 'MARTEX GLOBAL' shop watermark and show a workshop with many other sewing machines; dealer stock photos.
None of the three is an industrial machine: all are portable domestic machines with built-in motors, no table, no separate clutch or servo motor.
No machine is shown powered on or stitching; no foot pedal or power cord shown clearly.

identity.kind: domestic electric sewing machine (portable, not industrial)

claims.evidence: Photos 0, 1 and 2 show three different portable domestic sewing machines, none industrial.

claims.claim: Used for sewing clothes and multipurpose uses
claims.evidence: No clip of any machine stitching.

risks.risk: It is not clear which of the three machines is being sold.
risks.proof: Photo of the one machine for sale with a handwritten code and today's date beside it.
risks.if_unproven: As the cheapest of the three domestic machines shown.

risks.risk: Machine does not run, motor or timing faulty, or skips stitches.
risks.proof: Clip running the machine with the foot pedal and sewing a line of straight and zigzag stitch on fabric.

risks.risk: Foot pedal, power cord, bobbin case or accessories missing.
risks.proof: Photo of the machine with its foot pedal, cord, bobbin case and presser feet laid out.
risks.if_unproven: As machine head only, no pedal.

risks.risk: European voltage model needing a step-down or converter.
risks.proof: Photo of the rating plate on the back or underside showing voltage.

proof_requests: Photo of the exact machine being sold with a handwritten code and date in shot.
Clip of that machine sewing straight and zigzag stitches on fabric.
Photo of the rating plate showing brand, model and voltage.
Photo of the foot pedal, cord and accessories included.
response.reason: The photos show used portable domestic electric sewing machines, not an industrial one, so it is priced at its worst case as the cheapest domestic machine shown, not working, until the seller shows which unit and that it sews.
